To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the relativistic effects are important in the semileptonic Λc decays and they should be taken into account in order to describe the available experimental data.
the Λc → nl νl decays are dominated by the P -wave contribution, the Λc →Λl νl decay is dominated by the S -wave one.

the form factors of the semileptonic Λc → Λ lνl and Λ c → nlνl baryon decays are calculated without extrapolation and additional model assumptions in the whole accessible region, that the predictions for the decay rates, asymmetry and polarization parameters agree with available experimental data, and that the relativistic effects in the baryon wave function transformation from the rest to the moving reference frame and the contribution of negative-energy states are systematically taken into consideration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of weak decays of Λc baryons in a relativistic quark-model approach.
a systematic study of the semileptonic Λc → Λℓνℓ and Λc → nℓνℯ decays within the relativistic quarks model.
the calculation of the form factors and the decay rates of semileptonic weak decays of Λc baryons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relativistic quasipotentials are the best choice to calculate the Λc semileptonic decay form factors and the corresponding observables.
the relativistic quasipotentials approach with the QED and QCD motivated potential is very successful in describing the Λc b-baryon decays.
the theoretical results for the semileptonic Λc decays obtained in the framework of relativistic quark models are in good agreement with available experimental data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can explain the data for the decay Λc → Λeνe, and that our predictions for the Λc → pμνμ and Λc → Σ0eνe decays are in a very good agreement with the data.

we have calculated the form factors for the Λc b → Λb lνl and Λb → n lνl transitions in the whole accessible region without extrapolation and additional model assumptions, and that the predictions are in good agreement with the available experimental data.

we have developed a relativistic model for the semileptonic Λc decays, where the form factors are calculated from first principles, and that we can predict all relevant quantities in a consistent way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Λc → Ξ0lνl decay is the most promising for studying the Λc b-baryon in the near future.
the relativistic quasipotentional approach provides a good tool for the study of the Λc semileptonic decay dynamics and can be applied to the analysis of the forthcoming experimental data.
relativistic effects in semileptonic baryon decays are important and cannot be ignored.
